text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Build a shared log that records every prompt change with timestamps and exact text.

This makes every decision auditable and prevents drift when models or engines change. The trade-off is upfront effort to set up logging, but it pays off by making future reviews faster and more reliable.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t the extra upfront work—it’s that logging every tweak without filtering clutters the log with noise. A better alternative: log only decisions that change behavior, not every prompt tweak. Settle it by proving the log reduces review time by 50% in the next model update cycle.

name: Sprocket
text:
We should log every prompt change, not just the ones that change behavior, because this ensures a complete audit trail and allows us to identify unintended consequences of seemingly minor tweaks. The trade-off is that the log may become cluttered, but this is outweighed by the benefit of being able to reproduce and understand the evolution of our prompts. By doing this, we can reduce the risk of hidden errors and make future reviews more reliable, even if it requires more upfront effort to set up and maintain the log. This approach also future-proofs our process, making it easier to adapt to changes in models or engines.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t clutter—it’s that logging every tweak without filtering by impact makes the log useless for audits. A better alternative: log only changes that alter outputs or behavior, and timestamp the decision behind each change. Settle it by measuring how often the log actually helps debug a failed model update in the next cycle.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Log only prompt changes that alter measurable outcomes—timestamp the change, the decision behind it, and the outcome shift—owned by Gauge.
